Subject: Admin trace export: preferred transport and retention window

Olga — thanks for the call earlier. To move forward with the SOC 2 evidence pull we need a clear statement on how Redwood can deliver admin activity traces and what retention windows are available for customer-scope exports. Crestline prefers an automated delivery (SFTP push or presigned S3) and an immutable manifest with checksums and a signed HMAC. Questions we have up front: 

- What export transports do you support for on-demand and scheduled pulls? (SFTP push, SFTP pull, presigned S3, HTTPS POST to our ingestion endpoint)
- Can you provide per-operator CSV + JSONL formats for the exported events? Typical fields we require: timestamp (UTC), actor_id, action, target, resource_id, ip_address (if present), session_id, kv_cache_tokens (if applicable), and a redactable payload indicator.
- What retention windows are available for customer-requested snapshots vs your default retention? We need to confirm a 90/180/365 day policy depending on plan.
- How do you handle chain-of-custody and attestation? Crestline requires a signed manifest (SHA256 + HMAC) and a delivery log that shows push timestamp and recipient IP.

Please attach a sample export (small) with checksum so our audit team can validate ingestion. If you prefer, Neal from CipherAudits (copied) can accept the bundle on our behalf.

Best,
Markus
Director, IT Compliance
Crestline Health

Markus — thanks, this is straightforward. Summarizing options and our constraints so you can pick what fits your ingestion pipeline. Short answer: we support all four transports you listed; we recommend SFTP push or presigned S3 for large archives and HTTPS POST for single-file attestations. Details below and I attached a tiny sample export and checksum manifest.

Export transports and notes:
- SFTP push (preferred for scheduled/recurring snapshots): Redwood can push tar.gz packages to a customer-managed SFTP endpoint. We record transfer ok/fail in the delivery log and include signed manifest (SHA256 + HMAC).
- SFTP pull: we can expose a temporary SFTP endpoint for your team to pull; typically used for one-off forensic pulls.
- Presigned S3 URLs: For automated ingestion we can push the package to a Redwood S3 bucket and share presigned GET links (7–14 day TTL configurable). We can also issue presigned PUTs if you prefer to pull and store on your side.
- HTTPS POST to your ingestion endpoint: small payloads (<= 200 MB) can be POSTed to a customer endpoint over mutual TLS. We can rotate client certs per transfer.

Format and content:
- Primary bundle: tar.gz containing admin_activity_manifest_v1.csv (summary), admin_events.jsonl (line-delimited events), and export-sample-checksum.txt (manifest). Sample fields in CSV header: utc_ts,actor_id,actor_email,action_type,target_type,target_id,resource_path,ip,session_id,trace_id,redaction_flag,notes. JSONL entries include full event context for rows where redaction_flag==false.

Retention and snapshot windows:
- Hosted (default): 90 days rolling for raw admin events; 365 days aggregate metadata retained for billing/usage.
- Dedicated & Enterprise (contracted): options for 180 or 365 day data retention for customer-scoped exports; we can provide a time-limited snapshot (point-in-time) that you keep offsite.
- On-demand snapshot TTLs: presigned S3 links default to 7 days; we can extend to 30 days for contract customers. For longer-term storage we recommend you ingest to your archive and confirm checksum.

Chain-of-custody and attestation:
- Each bundle includes: export-sample-checksum.txt (file list + SHA256), manifest-signed.txt (base64 HMAC-SHA256 using Redwood signing key), and delivery-log.csv (push timestamp UTC, transfer method, recipient endpoint/IP, Redwood operator id).
- We can produce a notarized attestation (signed PDF) for legal if required — add-on service.

Redaction and PII considerations:
- Operator identifiers are included; we can pseudonymize actor_email on request and map to token IDs in a separate mapping file (only provided under NDAs).
- For SIG/CAIQ evidence pulls, we can provide a redacted sample plus a sealed mapping for auditors. Discuss if your auditors must see raw PII.

Next steps: if you confirm transport preference and retention window (90/180/365) we will schedule a small sample push to Neal's ingestion endpoint for validation. Proposed window: sample push Monday 11/09, full snapshot available 11/12 if approved.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Senior Manager, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

Technical note on exports and deltas — internal ops perspective:

- Daily delta export is supported and is our recommended pattern for ongoing compliance validation. Deltas include only events since last snapshot; each delta bundle contains a small manifest referencing the prior snapshot hash so you can chain-verify.
- For event fidelity: we include sequence numbers and trace_id to allow reassembly. If Crestline requires full re-playability (forensic reconstruction), we will deliver a point-in-time full snapshot plus deltas for continuity.
- Performance: for Dedicated customers we can produce full-day snapshots within a 2–4 hour window post-cut; for Hosted orgs, large tenant snapshots may be queued during off-peak and could take up to 24 hours.
- Redaction: automated PII redaction runs as an optional step; once redacted the mapping file is only accessible under an NDLA and specific auditor access.
- HMAC signing: we rotate the HMAC signing key monthly; we will include the key id and signature in manifest-signed.txt. Verification libraries (Python/Go) are in our compliance repo.

Action items: Markus/Neal — provide the ingestion endpoint (SFTP host/IP or HTTPS URL) and a preferred retention window. We will schedule a test delta push Wednesday 11/11.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Platform Observability
Redwood Inference
